identifierPolicy: A ground identifier is minted by this corpus and bound to the sentence of the list message that fixed it by sha256 over its bytes. The messages carry no identifiers, and a criterion number names a paragraph rather than a ground.
note: A member is one intake record, judged with the bytes under its root when it names one. Each reject member is refused under exactly one ground and every ground has a member that must be admitted, so a reader that refuses every record scores zero. Criterion 13 carries no ground: the criteria name no implementation, and these vectors, not any reader, are the shared test.

requirements.sentence: Every member of the admitted population is pinned by a digest over its exact bytes
a corpus digest covers the full tree together with its manifest
A reader refuses any member whose bytes do not match the pin.
The record carries a closed manifest of unique case or report identifiers, checked in both directions.
(i) missing from the population
(ii) duplicated
returned member outside the declared population is refused
an unexpected member inside a package declared complete
The boundary is declared before the check
Alongside the digest the record names which members were selected, by what expression, and how many matched.
A selection resolving to zero reports
or to more than one where exactly one is required, is refused at intake rather than silently bound
The per-case lines, the aggregate line and the exit code are all carried, so the finding does not rest on one line.
The printed total is one more value compared against the recount; any divergence is a refusal with both numbers recorded.
The reader recounts outcomes from the per-case records and never takes a printed summary line as the result.
For each refusal the record names the decision rule and the exact inputs it was recomputed from

the pinned record
bytes, including the carried per-case lines, aggregate line and exit code
named in this criterion
Native verdicts, reasons and process status are carried unchanged.
Native verdicts, reasons and process status are carried unchanged.
For each observation the record states one of three states: carried inline, referenced by digest, or absent.
An observation declared inline and not present is a fail-closed refusal.

The submitter declares an anchor carrying enough data to distinguish an availability failure (the reference does not resolve) from an integrity failure (it resolves but the digest does not match), and names the verdict for each.
the reference does not resolve
it resolves but the digest does not match
The checker is named by an immutable source revision and the exact command run
with runtime and dependencies named rather than inherited from whichever reader ran first
Any helper script, fixture fetcher or other artifact acquired at run time is named by both its acquisition URI and a content digest
an unresolvable helper or a digest mismatch is a refusal, never a silent fallback.

The submitter also states the reader's relationship to the reference
  implementation - the same implementation, reference-derived code, or
  an implementation written from the specification

identifies any
  shared verification code relevant to that distinction

no reader written from the specification has yet been run against the
Ed25519/JCS corpus, and the v2.1 record will say so as an explicit field.
The encoding identifier is drawn from a closed set, and a reader that does not implement the declared encoding rejects the record.
Every digest offered as evidence declares its exact input serialization; a digest whose input serialization is undeclared stays outside the record.

Byte identity - the same bytes always produce the same digest - and replay stability - the same pinned inputs produce byte-identical output across independent processes - are separate claims and are recorded separately.

the record
  declares the ordering used and the seed settings where applicable

Where raw outputs differ, that difference
  is retained even when a separately declared comparison of results
  agrees.

Output that varies across processes with no declared cause is
  a refusal.
The record states whether the expected answers were visible to the implementer before the run.
Reproducing recorded answers and detecting an injected fault are separate claims kept in separate records, even when one suite produces both
each deliberate fault has its own result, separate from the reproduction result and the exposure declaration.
Pair each relaxed-check result with its baseline

A FAIL that persists
  with a different refusing ground is not an unchanged native result

where another ground can still reject the object, that control alone
  does not isolate the relaxed check.
The record states what the suite establishes and what it leaves open.

It does not claim coverage of the whole attack surface, does not rank implementations, makes no claim about threats outside the corpus, and does not establish that an action happened or that its actor had authority
